DemandCast
ML Ratchet · GridSim phase 2 · trained on physics, graded on reality

DemandCast

Tomorrow's hourly electricity demand, wind and solar output for eight US grids, from the weather and the calendar, with error bars. The network never saw a real grid while it learned. It trained on 40,000 simulated region-days built from building heat-transfer physics and wind- and solar-farm physics, then sat an exam on 2023–2025.

Lab · real exam days

Change tomorrow's weather and watch the grid answer

Pick a grid and a day from the exam years. The sliders change the weather the forecast is given. The building model recomputes heating, cooling, lighting and rooftop solar for every hour, the farm physics recompute wind and solar output, and the network (running in your browser) turns those into a forecast with a 95 % band. The black line is what really happened; the dashed purple line is the grid operator's own day-ahead forecast.

Ratchet

Every rung, kept or not

A rung is kept only if it beats the incumbent on a frozen simulated validation set by more than 0.01 of skill (mean over demand, wind and solar of 1 − error / physics-alone error) and does not make the small real dev set (30 fixed-seed days per grid from 2019 and 2021) more than 2 % worse. When the simulator changed, every rung was re-scored on the new frozen set.

How it was built

Physics first, then a small network that corrects it

BuildingsHeat flows through each region's building stock: UA × (setpoint − effective temperature), with thermal mass (a fast and a slow RC lag), sun on walls and windows, internal gains and a spread of thermostat settings. Cooling adds latent load from humid air. Resistance heat, heat pumps (COP falls with cold) and AC (COP falls with heat) turn heat into MW. The calendar sets occupancy; daylight sets lighting; pvlib rooftop solar is netted out.
FarmsEvery EIA-860 wind farm and solar plant in the grid, switched on and off by its real dates. Wind: hub-height speed from the measured 10 m/50 m shear, moist-air density, a pitch-regulated farm power curve from specific power, wake, availability and electrical losses. Solar: pvlib with tracking or fixed tilt, cell temperature, clipping.
Simulated regionsReal 2018, 2020 and 2022 weather, perturbed (warmer, cooler, cloudier, windier), drives random building stocks and re-scaled real fleets. Demand gets real residual noise from training-year fits; wind and solar get weather errors and reporting-scale drift sized to match dev-year mismatch. Half the days get day-ahead forecast errors.
NetworkThree small MLPs (two hidden layers of 512, about 1.2 million weights in all). Inputs: the physics forecast for tomorrow split into components, the last week of real output against the physics, weather and calendar. Outputs: 24 hourly corrections and their uncertainty, trained with a Gaussian likelihood. No real grid data is ever a training example.

Where it falls short

    Use it

    The release

    demandcast-v1.0.zip holds a numpy-only model (demandcast.py, weights in one .npz), the dev-fitted physics priors per grid, a demo on real exam days that runs in seconds, a model card and every training script.

    python3 demo.py                        # 16 real exam days: DemandCast vs the grid's own forecast
python3 -c "import demandcast as dc; m = dc.DemandCast(); print(m.predict_demand(x))"
